questions.stem: Why is glucose present in the glomerular filtrate but not normally found in urine?

options.text: Glucose is too large to enter the filtrate
Glucose is destroyed by enzymes in the nephron
Glucose is reabsorbed back into the blood in the proximal convoluted tubule
Glucose is converted into urea before reaching the bladder

questions.explanation: Glucose is small enough to be filtered into Bowman's capsule during ultrafiltration, but it is a useful substance so it is completely reabsorbed back into the blood by active transport in the proximal convoluted tubule.
